scenarios.name: Hero Section Display and Value Proposition
scenarios.description: Verify the hero section displays product name, tagline, description, and primary call-to-action button that clearly communicates MirDB's value proposition (REQ-1, US-1)

steps.description: Load the MirDB product homepage in a browser
steps.context: User lands on the homepage from search, link, or direct navigation

steps.description: Check that the hero section contains product name 'MirDB', a clear tagline, and descriptive text explaining the core value proposition
steps.context: The hero section should be immediately visible without scrolling (above the fold)

steps.description: Confirm the presence of a primary call-to-action button that directs users to get started or learn more
steps.context: The CTA should be visually prominent and clearly actionable

test_cases.input: Load homepage and inspect hero section
test_cases.expected: Hero section displays 'MirDB' product name prominently
Tagline communicates 'persistent Memcached-compatible key-value store' value proposition

test_cases.input: Verify CTA button presence and functionality
test_cases.expected: Primary CTA button is visible, clickable, and navigates to appropriate destination

test_cases.input: Check hero section visibility without scrolling
test_cases.expected: Hero section is fully visible above the fold on standard viewport sizes

scenarios.name: Key Features Section Display
scenarios.description: Verify the features section presents MirDB's key features (Memcached compatibility, persistence, LSM architecture) in a scannable format (REQ-2, US-2)

steps.description: Scroll to or navigate to the features section of the homepage
steps.context: Features should be accessible from the main navigation or by scrolling

steps.description: Check that Memcached protocol compatibility is clearly highlighted with explanation
steps.context: This is a primary differentiator for MirDB

steps.description: Check that data persistence capability is highlighted and explained
steps.context: Persistence distinguishes MirDB from in-memory memcached

steps.description: Check that LSM tree architecture is mentioned with brief explanation
steps.context: Technical users will appreciate understanding the storage engine design

test_cases.expected: Features section is visible with grid or card-based layout
Feature card/section displays Memcached protocol compatibility with brief explanation
Feature card/section displays data persistence capability with explanation
Feature card/section displays LSM tree architecture with brief explanation
Feature mentions Tokio-based async performance for high-concurrency workloads
Features are presented in easily scannable format (cards, grid, or list with clear headings)

scenarios.name: Quick Start Code Examples
scenarios.description: Verify the quick-start section includes working code examples showing connection and basic operations (REQ-3, US-3)

steps.description: Scroll to or navigate to the quick-start section of the homepage
steps.context: Quick-start should enable first successful connection within 5 minutes

steps.description: Check that code examples are displayed with proper syntax highlighting
steps.context: Code blocks should use syntax-highlighted formatting

steps.description: Check that code blocks have copy-to-clipboard functionality
steps.context: Users should be able to easily copy code examples

steps.description: Ensure examples show server start, connection, SET, and GET operations
steps.context: Examples should cover basic CRUD operations

test_cases.expected: Quick-start section is visible with code examples
Code block shows './mirdb -c mirdb.toml' or equivalent server start command
Code block shows how to connect (telnet localhost 12333 or client library)
Code block shows SET command with expected STORED response
Code block shows GET command with expected VALUE response
Clicking copy button copies code to clipboard and shows confirmation
Code blocks display with proper syntax highlighting (bash/shell)

scenarios.name: Architecture Overview Section
scenarios.description: Verify the architecture section displays a visual diagram showing LSM tree data flow with explanations (REQ-4, US-5)

steps.description: Scroll to or navigate to the architecture section of the homepage
steps.context: Architecture section is a 'Should' priority requirement

steps.description: Check that an architecture diagram (SVG or image) is displayed
steps.context: Diagram should show LSM tree data flow

steps.description: Check that diagram shows Write -> WAL -> Memtable -> SSTable levels flow
steps.context: Technical users should understand the data path

steps.description: Check that brief explanations accompany the diagram
steps.context: Diagram should be understandable without extensive prior knowledge

test_cases.expected: Architecture section is visible with visual diagram
SVG or image diagram is displayed without errors
Diagram includes Write-Ahead Log (WAL) in the data flow
Diagram includes Memtable component in the data flow
Diagram includes SSTable levels in the data flow
Diagram image/SVG has descriptive alt text for accessibility
